That's essentially R1. Is that allowed? It is one coherent evidence objective. But maybe need not select another requirement. Fine.

We need preserve roles. Parent requirement source span mentions pack of downloadable content released for strategy video game over three years after its release. However no substantive part supported, so choose one faithful low-commitment facet. Could be just "Establish the identity of the downloadable content pack referenced by the Parent Requirement." Then later can establish timing. But the parent requirement's core is timing. The instruction says if no substantive part supported, still choose one faithful, low-commitment facet. So perhaps choose "Establish the identity of the downloadable content pack that is the subject of the Parent Requirement." That's low commitment and avoids bundling. But does that help? The parent requirement is about a DLC pack released for strategy game over three years after. The unknown entity may itself be residual target. Yes. We can target the DLC pack identity. But then local_residual should be "Establish the identity of the downloadable content pack described in the Parent Requirement." That is a coherent part. However the parent requirement is not just identity; it's release relation. But if no claims, we can start with identity. It doesn't add outside knowledge. It's faithful. Used claims [].

Need output JSON exactly. Ensure parent_requirement_id R1. mode probe. used_claims [] local_residual string.
